entries.clue: Aussie native won, overthrowing leader in fight (6)

indicatorNotes.overthrowing: W knocks the first letter off its perch and takes its place

blocks.note: W = won, as in sports results tables
COMBAT (fight) with its leader C replaced

annotation.surface: An Australian competitor wins a bout by toppling the champion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Aussie native' reads like a person, but it is an animal: the wombat is a burrowing Australian marsupial.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a burrowing marsupial found only in Australia is literally an Aussie native, though the phrase sounds like a person.

entries.clue: Order brew in a drinking establishment (4,3)

indicatorNotes.Order: to order letters is to arrange them afresh

annotation.surface: Someone orders a beer at the pub.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a customer asking for a drink, which suits the pub picture perfectly; here it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A wine bar is a place where drinks are served.

entries.clue: Biblical figure some condemned at foot of cross (5)

indicatorNotes.condemned: something condemned is wrecked, so its letters are knocked about
indicatorNotes.at foot of: the foot of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: A figure from the Bible, with the condemned at the foot of the cross, evokes the Crucifixion.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls toward the Gospels, but the figure is from the Old Testament.
annotation.definitionFit: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt in the Bible.

entries.clue: Suggests tall dudes remove their hats (7)

indicatorNotes.remove their hats: a word's hat is its first letter, so both words lose theirs

annotation.surface: Etiquette advice: it is recommended that tall men take off their hats indoors.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'hats' are the first letters of the two words right before them.
annotation.definitionFit: To allude is to suggest indirectly.

entries.clue: Very happy due to change in plan (4,2)

indicatorNotes.to change: DUE is to change its letters
indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters go inside MAP

blocks.note: a map is a plan, of a building for instance

annotation.surface: Someone is delighted because the plan has been altered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Made up' is British informal for delighted, especially in the north of England. 'Plan' as a noun gives MAP, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: Being 'made up' about something means being thrilled by it.

entries.clue: Missing worker infected by animal disease (6)

indicatorNotes.infected by: the disease gets inside the worker

blocks.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker
BSE, mad cow disease, goes inside ANT

annotation.surface: A worker is off sick after catching something from livestock.
annotation.walkthrough: BSE (bovine spongiform encephalopathy) is 'mad cow disease', a major British news story of the 1990s.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a pupil missing from the register is marked as not present.

entries.clue: Passing border in record time heading left (9)

indicatorNotes.heading: the heading of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: an EP (extended play) is a record
a hem is the border of a garment
an era is a period of time

annotation.surface: An athlete crosses a boundary in record time, then turns left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like movement across the border, but it is the definition: fleeting. The pieces are read in answer order, not clue order.
annotation.definitionFit: Something ephemeral is passing, lasting only briefly.

entries.clue: Advertisement boards trimmed and put on display (7)

indicatorNotes.boards: AD boards PARED as a passenger boards a train, getting inside

annotation.surface: Billboards were cut down to size and then shown off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advertisement boards' reads as billboards, but 'boards' is a verb: the AD climbs aboard PARED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: marching something past an audience is showing it off.

entries.clue: Doctor Dolittle with giant bird (4-6,3)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor something is to tamper with it

annotation.surface: Doctor Dolittle, who talks to animals, is seen with an enormous bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Dolittle' reads as the fictional vet, and 'giant bird' as one creature; in fact 'Doctor' is the instruction and 'giant' is fodder. The long-tailed tit is a tiny bird, the opposite of giant.
annotation.definitionFit: The long-tailed tit is a small European songbird.

entries.clue: Individuals in population estimates (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the next words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

annotation.surface: Census figures count individual people.
annotation.walkthrough: populati(ON ES)timates: the answer spans the join between the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Individual items or people are 'ones', as in 'the ones I like'.

entries.clue: Greatest part played in his role as one coming out (5,5)

indicatorNotes.played: played letters are performed in a new arrangement
indicatorNotes.coming out: the I comes out of the fodder

blocks.note: one = I, the Roman numeral; it is removed from the fodder

annotation.surface: An actor plays a character who comes out of the closet.
annotation.walkthrough: Remove one I from INHISROLEAS and the remaining ten letters rearrange to the answer. 'Part played' tempts you to read 'part' as a theatrical role.
annotation.definitionFit: The lion's share is the largest portion of something.

entries.clue: Humiliated and embarrassed after husband leaves (6)

indicatorNotes.leaves: a husband who leaves walks out, so his letter departs from the word

annotation.surface: A spouse walks out, leaving someone humiliated and embarrassed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as walking out of a marriage; here it takes H out of ABASHED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean brought low in dignity or self-respect.

entries.clue: Moon’s gravity may need to be adjusted (8)

indicatorNotes.to be adjusted: the letters need adjusting into a new order

annotation.surface: Calculations for the Moon's gravity might need correcting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moon' seems to be our own moon; it is the definition, a different one. 'Moon’s' means 'Moon is', linking definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Jupiter's largest satellite, the biggest in the solar system, is one moon among many.

entries.clue: Engineer and master mechanic? (9)

indicatorNotes.Engineer: to engineer something is to construct it, here from rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A job title: engineer and master mechanic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a job title alongside 'mechanic', but it is a verb telling you to rebuild AND MASTER. The question mark marks mechanic as one example of a tradesman.
annotation.definitionFit: A mechanic is one kind of tradesman, a skilled manual worker.

entries.clue: Boy turned right, fleeing alien, and spotted one with four legs (9)

indicatorNotes.turned: a boy who has turned faces the other way, so his letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.fleeing: something fleeing runs away, so R leaves the word it was in

annotation.surface: A boy turns and runs from an alien, then sees a four-legged animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right' sounds like a direction to turn; it is the letter R leaving MARTIAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the dog breed famous for its black-spotted white coat is a spotted thing with four legs.

entries.clue: Poke with end of sharp stick (4)

indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its final letter

annotation.surface: Jab at something with the pointed end of a stick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'End of sharp stick' reads as the pointy tip; the 'end' applies only to SHARP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean jabbing at something with a finger or pointed object.

entries.clue: Just over 50 in US city (4)

indicatorNotes.in: 50 is located in the city, so its letter sits inside the city's letters

blocks.note: o = over, the cricket scorebook abbreviation
L = 50 in Roman numerals, placed inside NY

annotation.surface: Slightly more than fifty in an American city, perhaps a temperature or a population.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Just over' reads as a phrase; split it, and 'Just' is the definition while 'over' gives O. In cricket an over is a set of six balls.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Just' and 'only' both mean merely.

entries.clue: Nothing upsets snuggling love birds (7)

indicatorNotes.snuggling: RILES snuggles around the O, holding it inside

blocks.note: love = O, zero in tennis; goes inside RILES

annotation.surface: Nothing bothers a pair of cuddling lovebirds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Love birds' reads as one romantic phrase; split it, and love is O while birds is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Orioles are brightly coloured songbirds.

entries.clue: Baby bird ran away at last clutching fish (9)

indicatorNotes.at last: the last letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: a ling is a fish of the cod family

annotation.surface: A young bird finally escaped while holding a fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clutching' looks like a container indicator; it only supplies its last letter G.
annotation.definitionFit: A fledgling is a young bird just learning to fly.

entries.clue: Tramp reflecting on unfinished clue for ‘swimmer’ (7)

indicatorNotes.reflecting: a reflection shows PLOD back to front

blocks.note: to tramp is to plod, walk heavily

annotation.surface: A vagrant muses over a half-written crossword clue whose answer is 'swimmer'.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun, a vagrant; it is a verb, to plod. In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the tramp comes first.
annotation.definitionFit: A dolphin is a sea mammal and a strong swimmer.

entries.clue: Pasta with American beans (7)

blocks.note: a kind of pasta, in long thin strips
bean and noodle are both slang for the head, noodle chiefly in the US

annotation.surface: A dish of pasta served with American-style beans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beans' reads as food beside the pasta; it is slang for heads, and so are noodles in American English.
annotation.definitionFit: Noodles are pasta, and in US slang a noodle is a head, as is a bean.

entries.clue: Small lake in view (6)

indicatorNotes.in: a lake in a view is inside the scene, so its letter sits inside the view's letters

blocks.note: L = lake, as on maps; placed inside SIGHT

annotation.surface: A little lake comes into view.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Small lake' looks like one description; 'Small' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a slight difference or a small one.

entries.clue: Cheated Harry involved in submitted lawsuit (8)

indicatorNotes.involved in: NAG is involved in, placed inside, FILED

blocks.note: to file a lawsuit is to submit it
to harry is to nag, pester

annotation.surface: A man named Harry cheated and got caught up in a court case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb to harry, to pester.
annotation.definitionFit: To finagle is to obtain something by trickery, so finagled = cheated.

entries.clue: Hide from source of loud beastly sound that is piercing (3,3)

indicatorNotes.source of: the source of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.piercing: IE pierces the other letters, sitting inside them

blocks.note: a low is the sound a cow makes
i.e. = that is; it pierces L+LOW after the L

annotation.surface: Take cover from a loud piercing animal noise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piercing' reads as describing a shrill noise, which suits 'loud beastly sound'; it is a container instruction, and the beast here is a cow.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to stay out of sight and avoid notice is to hide.

entries.clue: Top 40 on the radio (5)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: on the radio you hear sounds, not spellings

blocks.note: XL = 40 in Roman numerals, said as 'ex-ell'

annotation.surface: A chart show: the Top 40 on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Top 40' reads as the pop chart; 'Top' is the verb, to beat or surpass.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to top a rival is to outdo them, to be the best.

entries.clue: Aloof second-in-command departs, relaxing aboard marine glider (6,4)

indicatorNotes.second-in-command: the second letter in COMMAND, O
indicatorNotes.departs: an officer who departs leaves the ship, so that letter leaves the word
indicatorNotes.aboard: LYING goes aboard, inside, what is left

blocks.note: the second letter of COMMAND is removed from OFFISH

annotation.surface: A standoffish deputy leaves the ship, relaxing aboard a seaplane.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second-in-command' reads as a deputy officer; it is literally the second letter in 'command'.
annotation.definitionFit: Flying fish leave the water and glide through the air on wing-like fins.

entries.clue: It’s below the knee – a little lower (4)

blocks.note: the fleshy back of the leg between knee and ankle
a lower is something that lows (moos), so a little one is a young cow

annotation.surface: Something sits below the knee, a bit further down the leg.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as 'further down'; it is one who lows, that is, moos.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a part of the lower leg by description, and a crossword-only coinage where 'lower' means a mooing animal, whose young one fits.

entries.clue: Soprano, working with a tenor and alto, produces music (6)

blocks.note: on = working, as a switched-on machine

annotation.surface: A soprano, a tenor and an alto perform a piece together.
annotation.walkthrough: The voice parts are abbreviated as in SATB choral scores.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a composition for one or two instruments in several movements is one kind of music.

entries.clue: Cryptic clues about new family members (6)

indicatorNotes.about: the rearranged CLUES go about N

annotation.surface: Puzzling hints about babies joining the family.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nods at the crossword itself: 'Cryptic clues' is exactly what the solver is reading. 'New family members' suggests babies, but uncles need not be new.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a parent's brothers are one kind of relative.
